title: The Handover Defect
brief: Two months after handover of a Meridian Build school extension, the client reports water entering at 4 windows in the new classrooms. They ask for a response within 5 working days. You have 12 visit points to contain, find the cause, and respond.

actions.label: Other projects with the same window system
General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Inspection and test plan for windows
Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Defect report DR-15 logged on the day with photos and an owner.
The same window system and installer were used on 2 other handed-over projects; no one has checked them.
evidence.whyItMatters: Containment includes other output built the same way.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask where else the method was used.

evidence.text: Handover inspection records are signed by the client.
Water test records: ITP requires testing 10 percent of windows; 2 of 48 windows were tested (record WT-1).
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare tested quantity with the plan.

evidence.text: Window installer records show a change of sealant product (SL-9 to SL-12) mid-project; not reviewed by Meridian Build.
evidence.whyItMatters: Changes by external providers must be controlled.

evidence.text: Installer: "Head flashing wasn't on our drawing, so we sealed only." Drawing W-12 revision A lacks the head flashing shown in revision B. (note 3)
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask what the installer worked from.

evidence.text: ITP section 4 for windows does not name who witnesses water tests.
evidence.whyItMatters: Clearer roles would strengthen the test.

evidence.text: Aftercare procedure requires a response in 5 working days.
Snag list was closed with client sign-off.
Window head W-3 shows no flashing, consistent with drawing W-12 revision A.
A classroom notice board shows a hand-drawn sign about the leak.
evidence.whyItMatters: An informal sign by the client is not a nonconformity.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The client's sign is not a finding.

evidence.text: Frame paint colour slightly differs from the sample, within the agreed tolerance.

decisions.prompt: What should the response to the client include?
options: A note that the client signed handover
Temporary protection of the classrooms, the cause found so far, permanent repair plan with dates, inspection of all windows, and a contact
A request that the client calls the installer
An offer of a discount only
decisions.rationale: Handover sign-off does not end the obligation to correct defects.

containment: Protect the affected classrooms and inspect the other 2 projects with the same system
correction: Install head flashing per revision B and retest windows
cause: Installer worked from an old drawing, sealant change was not reviewed, and water testing fell short of the ITP
corrective: Issue drawings to subcontractors through the register, review subcontractor material changes, and enforce ITP test quantities
effectiveness: Water test 10 percent of windows on the next three projects with witnessed records

debriefText.found: You extended containment to other projects.
debriefText.missed: Ask which drawing the subcontractor actually used.
debriefText.falseFinding: A colour within tolerance is conforming.
